title: Overhead-Guided Instrumentation Refinement
problem: Instrumentation incurs significant runtime overhead that skews performance analysis results. The challenge is automatically selecting which functions to instrument to maximize measurement coverage while staying within a user-defined overhead budget.
motivation: Excessive instrumentation overhead invalidates performance measurements, requiring a balance between measurement coverage and accuracy.
method: The approach selects which functions to measure by framing it as an optimization problem (binary knapsack: choosing items for a limited-capacity backpack). It uses two sources of information: runtime measurements from actually running the program, and static information about how functions call each other in the code structure. Based on these, it estimates the measurement overhead for each function and automatically selects the set that maximizes visibility into hot spots (where execution time is spent) without exceeding the overhead budget. The method was implemented in the PIRA profiling infrastructure and evaluated on HPC proxy applications including LULESH, AMG2013, MILC, and ASTAR.
key_novelty: An optimization approach automatically selects which functions to instrument, maximizing visibility of program hot spots while staying within a measurement overhead budget.
contributions: Binary knapsack formulation for instrumentation optimization
Integration of dynamic and static analysis for cost estimation
Demonstration on HPC applications achieving coverage within overhead limits
